headline: Leasing and capital markets drive broad margin expansion
summary_short: JLL reported Q2 FY2026 revenue of $6,927.9M, up 10.8% y/y (10% in local currency), as Leasing Advisory (+24%) and Capital Markets Services (+19%) led growth; net income attributable to common shareholders rose to $215.6M ($4.59 diluted EPS) from $112.3M ($2.32) a year ago.
summary_long: Revenue grew 10% in local currency, led by Advisory revenue (+21%): Leasing Advisory (+24%, on office/industrial/data-center momentum in the U.S., Japan, UK) and Investment Sales/Debt-Equity Advisory (+25% ex-MSR, debt advisory +44%). Resilient revenue rose 8%, led by Workplace Management (+10%) on mandate expansions and new wins. Operating income rose 47% to $290.9M and Adjusted EBITDA rose 32% to $386.3M, driven by Capital Markets/Leasing growth, platform leverage, and the absence of a $14M prior-year Fannie Mae charge. Interest expense fell to $26.4M on lower borrowings and rate. Net income rose to $215.6M ($4.59 diluted EPS) from $112.3M. JLL repurchased $110.0M of stock in the quarter; $2,591.6M remains authorized. No numeric forward guidance was given.

drivers.explanation: Company states higher Adjusted EBITDA and margin were primarily driven by Capital Markets Services and Leasing Advisory on strong revenue growth and platform leverage, plus the absence of a $14M prior-year Fannie Mae loss-share charge.

Advisory revenue (+21%) led by Leasing Advisory (+24%, office/industrial/data-center momentum) and Investment Sales/Debt-Equity Advisory (+25% ex-MSR); Resilient revenue (+8%) led by Workplace Management (+10%, mandate expansions, new wins).

Tracks revenue growth outpacing a 9% rise in total operating expenses; gross contract costs rose with pass-through client mandates while platform costs rose mainly on commission expense tied to Advisory revenue growth.

Capital Markets Services and Leasing Advisory EBITDA grew fastest (+74% and +38%) on revenue growth net of higher commissions plus platform leverage; Capital Markets also benefited from the absence of the $14M prior-year Fannie Mae charge.

Company attributes the increase to the operating income and Adjusted EBITDA drivers above, plus lower interest expense on lower average borrowings and rate, partially offset by a higher income tax provision.
Tracks the net-income increase; diluted weighted-average shares fell to 46.925M from 48.334M y/y on continued buybacks, adding to per-share growth beyond the income increase alone.
Tracks the net-income increase on a basic share count that fell to 46.244M from 47.483M y/y on continued repurchases, including completion of a $200.0M accelerated share repurchase program.

Not directly reconciled in the release to a single cause; operating cash flow improved y/y on higher earnings, partially offset by higher trade receivables tied to revenue growth, per the Liquidity section.

Not explained directly in the release; equity rose on retained net income across the trailing year, partially offset by $410.0M of year-to-date share repurchases and foreign currency translation losses in AOCI.
